subject: [RFC PATCH 08/57] mm/collapse: scan a table for what a collapse could use

2026-08-16.patch_summary: This patch introduces a table scanning mechanism to identify potential candidates for memory collapsing. The scan walks through the page table and sets a bit in the cc->eligible_ptes bitmap for each present, anonymous, non-uffd-armed, LRU, and unlocked PTE that could be used as a source for collapse. The scan takes no page table lock and produces advisory results, which are later frozen under the lock to ensure correctness. The patch also addresses issues related to partial tables, swapped-out and shared PTEs, and folio reference counts. It provides a two-sided verdict: either a PMD candidate is selected or the whole table is refused if it exceeds certain limits.

reviews.author: Lance Yang
reviews.summary: Reviewer Lance Yang noted that the lockless accessor ptep_get() may return stale data on arm64 due to its lack of consistency retry, and suggested using the lockless variant ptep_get_lockless() instead.

reviews.author: Kiryl Shutsemau (author)
reviews.summary: The author is addressing a concern about using the wrong accessor for a walk that holds no lock, specifically ptep_get() instead of ptep_get_lockless(). They acknowledge this is an issue and plan to switch to ptep_get_lockless() in v2.
reviews.raw_body:
Good catch, thanks -- switched to ptep_get_lockless() for v2.

I don't think it would lead to any correctness issues: both variants
take the pfn and the protection bits from one __ptep_get() of the target
entry, so all contpte_ptep_get() can get wrong here is the young and
dirty bits it gathers from the neighbours.  The scan reads dirty only
for the lazyfree skip, which the freeze re-tests under the page table
lock, and young only as a hint.

But it is still the wrong accessor for a walk that holds no lock.

collapse_faultin_addr() already reads its entry with ptep_get_lockless().

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

2026-08-24.patch_summary: This patch adds a function to scan a page table and identify potential candidates for collapsing, which is a process of merging multiple pages into one. The function sets bits in the cc->eligible_ptes bitmap for every present, anonymous, non-UFFD-armed PTE that is on the LRU and unlocked. This advice is then used by the freeze to settle any questions about the collapse candidates. The patch also handles cases where a partial table is scanned and ensures that limits are applied per PMD, rather than globally.
